capabilities.title: Fine-tune a model with plain LoRA
capabilities.summary: Train low-rank adapters on a frozen base model and save only the adapter weights (~MBs).

when: Parameter-efficiently fine-tuning an LLM or diffusion model on a downstream task without touching all weights
The bf16/fp16 base model fits in GPU memory (memory is not the binding constraint)
No PEFT method has been chosen, or LoRA is the chosen default
avoid_when: The bf16 base + LoRA + optimizer state does not fit in VRAM — use QLoRA instead
The task is the RL/preference-optimization loop itself (PPO, DPO, reward models) — use trl (PEFT only supplies the adapter trl trains)

expected_outcomes: Performance comparable to full fine-tuning at a fraction of the compute, memory, and storage cost
Adapter checkpoint is tiny (e.g. ~19MB vs ~11GB for the full base model)

steps: Load the base model and tokenizer (e.g. AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained).
Build a LoraConfig with task_type matching the head (e.g. TaskType.CAUSAL_LM), plus r, lora_alpha, and target_modules; wrap the base with get_peft_model.
Call model.print_trainable_parameters() to confirm the adapter wrapped — the trainable fraction should be small (often <1%).
Train with the Transformers Trainer (or TRL SFTTrainer) exactly as you would the base model.
Save the adapter with model.save_pretrained(out_dir) — only the adapter weights are written.

validation: print_trainable_parameters() reports a small trainable fraction (often <1%), not 0
save_pretrained writes an adapter directory that is only ~MBs, not the size of the full model
The adapter reloads onto the base with PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, out_dir)
recovery: print_trainable_parameters() reports 0 trainable params -> the LoraConfig target_modules or task_type is wrong for this architecture
The adapter underfits -> raise r (start low, e.g. 8 or 16, and increase only if needed)

capabilities.title: LoraConfig core parameters (r, lora_alpha, target_modules, init)
capabilities.summary: The four knobs that govern every LoRA-family run — capacity, scaling, placement, initialization — and how to set them.

when: Building a LoraConfig for LoRA, DoRA, AdaLoRA, or a similar reparameterization adapter
Deciding rank, scaling factor, which modules to adapt, or weight initialization
avoid_when: Using a soft-prompt method (prompt/prefix/P-tuning) — those use their own config classes and num_virtual_tokens, not LoraConfig

steps: Set r, the rank of the update matrices A/B — common values 8/16/32/64; trainable-parameter count grows roughly linearly with r; start low and raise only if the adapter underfits.
Set lora_alpha, the scaling factor; the injected delta is scaled by lora_alpha/r; a common heuristic is lora_alpha = 2*r (e.g. r=16, lora_alpha=32).
Set target_modules to the module name suffixes to adapt (e.g. ["q_proj", "v_proj"]) or a regex string; if omitted, PEFT applies a model-type default (often the attention query/value projections).

Leave init_lora_weights=True for zero-init (B zeros, A Kaiming-uniform) so training starts from the unmodified base; use "gaussian" or PiSSA/OLoRA/LoftQ strings to initialize from a base-weight decomposition for faster convergence.

Optionally set task_type to match the head (CAUSAL_LM, SEQ_2_SEQ_LM, SEQ_CLS, TOKEN_CLS, QUESTION_ANS, FEATURE_EXTRACTION), lora_dropout for regularization, use_rslora for rank-stabilized scaling (lora_alpha/sqrt(r)) at higher ranks, use_dora to enable DoRA, and modules_to_save to fully train and save extra modules such as a fresh classifier head.

capabilities.title: Fit a large model on a small GPU with QLoRA (4-bit base + LoRA)
capabilities.summary: Load the frozen base in 4-bit, make it trainable, and train a full-precision LoRA adapter on top.

when: The full-precision/bf16 base + LoRA + optimizer state does not fit in GPU memory (e.g. a single <24GB GPU)
Training is memory-constrained and needs 4-bit/8-bit quantized base loading
avoid_when: Memory is not the constraint — use plain LoRA; 4-bit adds dequantization overhead and a more fragile k-bit grad path for no benefit
You will need to merge_and_unload the adapter into the base for inference — merging is not supported on a quantized base

steps: Confirm the precondition: the bf16 base + LoRA + optimizer state won't fit (otherwise use plain LoRA).

Build a BitsAndBytesConfig with load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4", bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True, and bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16 (torch.float16 on pre-Ampere; never leave it float32, which silently slows training); pass it via quantization_config to from_pretrained with device_map="auto".
Optionally call model.gradient_checkpointing_enable() for memory savings — do it BEFORE the next step.

Call model = prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model). This step is mandatory: skipping it is the most common QLoRA failure — the model 'trains' but loss stays flat because no gradient reaches the adapters.
Attach LoRA with get_peft_model(model, LoraConfig(...)) and call print_trainable_parameters().
Train, then save the adapter; keep the quantized base separate.

validation: print_trainable_parameters() reports well under 1% for a 7B base — not 0, and not an unexpectedly large count
Training loss decreases; a flat loss means prepare_model_for_kbit_training was skipped or was called after get_peft_model
recovery: Loss is flat / model 'trains' but does not learn -> prepare_model_for_kbit_training was skipped or run after get_peft_model; call it once right after loading the quantized base and before get_peft_model
0 trainable params or an unexpectedly large count -> the LoraConfig or preparation step is wrong
Training is unexpectedly slow -> bnb_4bit_compute_dtype was left at float32; set it to torch.bfloat16 (Ampere+) or torch.float16

prepare_model_for_int8_training is deprecated (0.4.0) -> use prepare_model_for_kbit_training; passing load_in_4bit/load_in_8bit directly to from_pretrained is deprecated (transformers 4.30) -> use BitsAndBytesConfig via quantization_config

capabilities.title: Choose a PEFT method
capabilities.summary: Decision boundaries for picking LoRA vs DoRA/AdaLoRA vs IA3/soft prompts vs QLoRA vs multi-GPU sharding.

when: A PEFT method has not yet been chosen
Deciding between adapter families given quality, parameter-budget, memory, and hardware trade-offs
avoid_when: The task is the RL/preference-optimization loop itself (PPO/DPO/reward models) — use trl
The task is high-throughput production serving of the merged model — use a dedicated inference engine such as vLLM

steps: Default to plain LoRA when no method is picked.

Choose DoRA or AdaLoRA for higher quality at slightly more cost: DoRA improves over LoRA at low ranks but is slower and uses more memory; AdaLoRA allocates a rank budget and requires setting total_step to the true number of optimizer steps.

Choose IA3 or a soft-prompt method when you need the fewest trainable params: prompt tuning is fewest/fastest, prefix tuning touches every layer for more capacity, multitask prompt tuning reuses source-task prompts, IA3 gives LoRA-like quality with fewer params and no merge into weights, and OFT/BOFT preserve base behavior (good for generative image models).
Choose QLoRA when the base model does not fit in VRAM on a single GPU.
For a model too large for one GPU even quantized with multiple GPUs available, choose DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 for the largest models and FSDP for medium models.

capabilities.title: Load and run inference with a trained adapter
capabilities.summary: Attach a saved adapter to its base model, optionally merge, and generate.

when: Running inference or deploying a model from a trained adapter checkpoint
Serving multiple tasks from one base by swapping adapters
avoid_when: High-throughput production serving of the merged model — use a dedicated inference engine such as vLLM
Merging via merge_and_unload on a quantized base — not supported (LoRA-family, non-quantized bases only)

expected_outcomes: merge_and_unload folds the adapter into the base weights for zero inference overhead

steps: Load the base model, or use AutoPeftModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained for one-call loading.
Attach the adapter with PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, adapter_path).
Optionally call merge_and_unload() to fold the adapter in for zero inference overhead — LoRA-family only, not on a quantized base.
To serve multiple tasks from one base, keep adapters separate and swap them with set_adapter instead of merging.
Run generate().

validation: generate() returns output on the adapter-attached model
If merged, the merged model produces the same outputs as the adapter-attached model before it is served
recovery: merge_and_unload fails on a quantized base -> do not merge; keep the adapter attached, or swap adapters with set_adapter

capabilities.title: Scale PEFT training across multiple GPUs (DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 / FSDP)
capabilities.summary: Drive sharded multi-GPU LoRA training through Accelerate plus a launch config.

when: The model is too large for one GPU even quantized and multiple GPUs are available
Training a large base (e.g. Llama-2-70B) with LoRA across GPUs
avoid_when: The model fits on one GPU (with or without QLoRA) — the sharding overhead is unnecessary

steps: Generate an Accelerate config with `accelerate config --config_file <name>.yaml`; pick ZeRO-3 (largest models) or FSDP (medium models) when prompted, and set zero_stage: 3 with zero3_save_16bit_model: true.

Launch with `accelerate launch --config_file <config> train.py --use_peft_lora True --lora_r 8 --lora_alpha 16 --lora_target_modules all-linear` plus standard SFT flags; SFTTrainer builds the PeftModel from peft_config and Accelerate wraps it into the DeepSpeed/FSDP engine on trainer.train().

For ZeRO-3 + QLoRA (e.g. 70B on 2x40GB), set num_processes: 2, drop gradient_accumulation_steps from the DeepSpeed block, add bnb_4bit_quant_storage to BitsAndBytesConfig matching the model load dtype, and pass --use_4bit_quantization True --use_nested_quant True --bnb_4bit_compute_dtype bfloat16 --bnb_4bit_quant_storage_dtype bfloat16; requires bitsandbytes>=0.43.3, accelerate>=1.0.1, transformers>4.44.2, trl>0.11.4, peft>0.13.0, and zero3_init_flag: true.
To train a large model on a single GPU, use ZeRO-3 CPU offload (offload_optimizer_device: cpu, offload_param_device: cpu, num_processes: 1).
Save the final model with trainer.save_model().

validation: zero3_save_16bit_model: true is set so the saved adapter weights are 16-bit and reloadable with from_pretrained
In a custom (non-Trainer) loop, ZeRO-3 is detected via accelerator.state.deepspeed_plugin.zero_stage == 3 before calling generate()
recovery: Saved adapter cannot be reloaded with from_pretrained -> confirm zero3_save_16bit_model: true in the config
ZeRO-3 + QLoRA version conflicts -> pin bitsandbytes>=0.43.3, accelerate>=1.0.1, transformers>4.44.2, trl>0.11.4, peft>0.13.0
